faqs.q: Can underfloor heating be installed under any floor covering?
faqs.a: Most floor coverings are compatible — tiles, stone, wood, vinyl, and carpet. Some engineered wood products have temperature limits; check the manufacturer's specification before installing underfloor heating beneath them.

faqs.q: How long does underfloor heating take to heat a room?
faqs.a: Wet systems are slower to respond than radiators — allow 2-4 hours to reach full temperature. This is why a programmable thermostat is essential: set it to pre-heat rooms before you need them.

faqs.q: Can underfloor heating be added to an existing home?
faqs.a: Yes. Low-profile retrofit systems (as thin as 15mm) can be installed without major floor height changes. Electric mat systems are the least invasive option for single rooms.

faqs.q: What warranty comes with underfloor heating?
faqs.a: Quality wet pipe systems carry 25-year manufacturer warranties. Electric mat systems typically carry 10-25 year warranties. The installation labour guarantee varies by contractor — ask for a minimum of 12 months.

The mixed water hardness found across the area presents an important consideration for wet underfloor heating installations, as fluctuating mineral content can gradually affect pipe performance and system efficiency over time — making proper inhibitor treatments and regular maintenance checks essential. Homeowners in Rosewood considering a switch from conventional radiators will find that underfloor heating integrates particularly well with well-insulated newer builds, while older properties may require additional groundwork to achieve comparable results. It is also worth noting that while Rosewood sits within South Ayrshire, some local contractors serving this area operate across a broader remit that includes Northern Ireland, giving residents access to experienced installers familiar with a wide range of property types, climates, and water quality conditions similar to those encountered locally.
whatItInvolves: Underfloor heating distributes heat evenly across the entire floor surface rather than from a single radiator point, eliminating cold spots and freeing up wall space. Wet systems (water pipes) connect to your existing boiler and are more efficient long-term. Electric mat systems are faster to install and suit smaller areas or retrofits where pipe runs aren't practical.
process: Wet system installation: survey the floor construction and calculate heat output requirements per room. Lay insulation boards to prevent heat loss downward. Install pipe circuits using the manifold as the central distribution point, connect to boiler flow and return. Commission and pressure test to 6 bar. Screed or dry lay over the top. The system must cure before the floor covering is laid — allow 21-28 days for screed.
whatToExpect: Underfloor heating runs at lower temperatures than radiators — typically 35-45°C flow temperature vs 70-80°C for radiators — which makes it significantly cheaper to run with a heat pump or condensing boiler. The system is slower to respond than radiators, so use a programmable thermostat to pre-heat rooms. Most manufacturers offer 25-year warranties on the pipe systems.
